messages:
Alex - Finance: Hey team, invoiced BrightHire for 2026-03-07. Invoice total looks right but their token usage in the metering ledger is 18.4M — we expected ~10M because they were hitting the org rate limit all day. Can someone confirm whether rate-limited requests still increment billable token counts? :thinking:
Maya - Billing: Which invoice # and org id? I can pull the ledger rows.
Alex - Finance: BH-2026-03-07 (link to invoice). Org: brighthire-prod (org_987). Metering shows spikes between 09:12-09:45 UTC.
metering-bot: Alert — unusual token spike for org 'brighthire-prod' on 2026-03-07 09:00-10:00 UTC. tokens=18432210, requests=24k, rate_limit_triggers=14k.
Priya - Eng Infra: Looking. Initial question: are you sure those 14k are rate-limit triggers (429) vs rejections at gateway? Our current pipeline increments token counters at the ingress stage, before rate-limit check — but we have a flag to dedupe repeated retries.
Maya - Billing: If tokens are counted before rate limiting, that's a problem — we might be charging for rejected attempts. We need clear rules: only successful responses (2xx + generated tokens) should be billable.
Priya - Eng Infra: Past behavior has been mixed. For streaming endpoints we count produced tokens on the backend writer. For legacy synchronous endpoints tokens are recorded when request enters model runner. I pulled the raw logs for brighthire timeframe, see snippet:
```
2026-03-07T09:14:03Z ingress service: req_id=abc123 org=org_987 method=chat.complete size=2048 tokens_est=512 status=429 rate_limit_group=org
2026-03-07T09:14:03Z ingress service: req_id=abc123 billing:tokens_recorded=512 ledger_row_id=lk_558
2026-03-07T09:14:05Z retry service: req_id=abc123 retry=1 forwarded_to_runner status=200 tokens_consumed=512
2026-03-07T09:14:05Z billing service: ledger_row_id=lk_558 updated status=consumed
```
Priya - Eng Infra: So: we initially write a provisional ledger row at ingress (to capture intent) and then update it when consumed. If a request is rejected and never forwarded, we mark it rejected and set billable=0. But retries can lead to duplicate provisional rows if dedupe fails.
Alex - Finance: That sequence suggests duplicates. Does ledger have dedupe by request id? Seems lk_558 updated, but I also see multiple provisional rows for same request_id in the full dump.
Priya - Eng Infra: We used to dedupe on client-provided idempotency keys, but some SDK versions didn't set them, and back-ported retries generated new ids. I'll run a query to find duplicate provisional rows for org_987 between 09:00-10:00.
Leo - Revenue Ops: While Priya digs in — would finance be comfortable issuing a temporary credit to BrightHire if we confirm they were overbilled? We should keep them from escalating.
Maya - Billing: Yes, if we confirm overbilling we can issue a corrective credit. Need exact amount and ledger rows to reverse. Also want to check whether the invoice system already aggregated deduped tokens or raw ledger entries.
Priya - Eng Infra: Quick findings: 3,412 provisional rows without finalization for org_987 in that hour, plus 2,900 duplicated provisional rows that later were deduped but still counted in an interim aggregate job. Looks like an old batch job that computed invoice tokens pulled provisional rows before finalization.
Alex - Finance: Oof. So the invoice job read a cache snapshot with provisional rows included. Can we produce a corrected token tally for that invoice? I need a delta to propose a credit.
Priya - Eng Infra: I'll export a corrected tally: count only ledger rows where status in (consumed, finalized) and ignore provisional_if_not_finalized. ETA 30m.
Maya - Billing: Great. If delta > $100 we'll prepare a credit memo template. If > $5k escalate to legal for customer notification plan.
Leo - Revenue Ops: Also recommend short-term: add a guard in invoicing job to only include finalized rows or to exclude provisional rows flagged by ingress_race=true. Low-risk quick fix.
Priya - Eng Infra: Agreed. I'll patch the invoicing snapshot job to filter on finalized=true and redeploy the job ASAP.
Alex - Finance: Thanks. One more ask: can we identify SDK versions used by brighthire during that hour? If older SDK caused missing idempotency keys we should surface upgrade guidance.
Priya - Eng Infra: Yes, logs include user_agent: BrightClient/1.2.0 and BrightClient/1.1.7 for 90% of requests. Those SDKs predate idempotency change. I'll include that in the export.
Maya - Billing: I'll hold the credit issuance until Priya's corrected delta arrives. Once we have the delta I'll draft the credit memo and ping legal if needed.
Alex - Finance: Sounds good. Please @here once export is ready and include the delta and affected invoice lines.
Priya - Eng Infra: Export done. Corrected token count for invoice BH-2026-03-07 is 9,965,412 tokens (previously 18,432,210). Delta = 8,466,798 tokens. I'll attach CSV to the ticket and file a rollback patch for the snapshot job.
Maya - Billing: Delta noted. Calculating credit now. Rough estimate at our rate = $0.0006/token => credit ~= $5,080.08. I'll confirm with precise pricing tiers.
Leo - Revenue Ops: FYI will draft a short customer note and offer opt-in early SDK migration support. :thumbsup:
Alex - Finance: Thanks everyone. Let's close after Maya posts final credit memo and Priya's fix is in prod.
Maya - Billing: Will send memo by EOD.
Priya - Eng Infra: Snapshot patch deployed to prod, and invoice job re-run for affected invoices.
Alex - Finance: Closing loop — thanks :raised_hands:
